key_insight: The paper shows that discrete log-concavity of the ground state is the structural bridge that lets adiabatic quantum optimization extend tunneling-based speedups from simple spike models to a broader class of convex and mildly nonconvex potentials.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers a new criterion for predicting when AQO may retain favorable spectral gaps and tunneling behavior beyond toy problems, informing more realistic optimization model selection.
method: Prove discrete log-concavity of ground states for a broad family of 1D discrete Schrödinger operators.
Use this structure to derive improved spectral gap bounds for convex potentials.
Extend Reichardt-style perturbative tunneling analysis from linear to quadratic spiked potentials.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical validation through new spectral gap bounds and a worked extension from the exactly solvable linear spike case to the non-solvable quadratic spike case.
watch_item: The results are theoretical and focused on 1D discrete models, so practical quantum advantage on higher-dimensional or noisy hardware remains unverified.
paper_title: Log-concavity and tunneling: adiabatic quantum optimization for convex functions (with a spike)
